objective: At the owner's request ('Then both yes', approving the round-plane epic with the radius-2 pattern set first, and a standing mandate to follow promising leads): ask what the pinwheel's own local law forces and what it can grow. The pinwheel's tile law has round bond-distance circles (PINWHEEL-ROUND-20261107-001) and is regrown by an eleven-label rule whose labels are read within radius 2 on tested patches (PINWHEEL-NATIVE-20261107-001; the rule is known in substance from Kenyon and Stephenson, Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 2019). Shared question with the sphere line (SPHERE-GROWTH-20261107-001): how much hidden information does roundness cost, and can growth replace it? A (proof): the complete radius-2 atlas of the pinwheel law, from a finite closure of collared tiles under the cut, so that labels are read within radius 2 on every pinwheel tiling. B (exploratory): whether a periodic plane satisfies the same radius-r law, the planar analogue of the tube lemma; if one does, the undecorated law cannot force roundness. C (exploratory): growth of the plane from one knot with the labels dropped, the growing boundary's shape the only memory: whether moves are forced, whether growth reaches dead ends, and whether it stays pinwheel. Serves question 9 (space from a law).
status: Complete 2026-11-07: the pinwheel's own law is a finite list of 1,168 radius-2 forms that fixes every label on every pinwheel tiling (proved), so regrowth needs no memory beyond the map (inside proved; at the boundary measured, levels 4-7); and no tested periodic plane obeys it even at radius 1 (exploratory). Outward growth held as backlog.
stop_rule: Stop when A's closure is verified or obstructed, B has tested its declared candidates and torus sizes, and C has run its declared growth trials to its declared radius or first unavoidable dead end; do not add candidates, radii or rules after seeing results.
title: The pinwheel's own law: what it forces and what it grows
